_help: HOW THE SHEDS ARE REALLY BUILT: the default construction numbers every building starts from.

A manufacturer file can change any of them (its 'construction' block), then a company can (its own 'construction' block), then the options the customer picks can (for example 12 in joists). Later wins.

Any value can be a plain value or a RULE LIST, first match wins: [{"when": {"maxW": 8}, "value": "2x4"}, {"value": "2x6"}]. 'when' may test minW maxW minL maxL (feet), styles (a list of style keys), roof (a roof shape or a list of them) and metal (true or false). The header rule tests maxSpanFt/minSpanFt, the width of the opening, and is picked per opening.
Numbers ending In are inches, Ft are feet. A number with no unit in its name is a count.
Everything a drawing depends on keeps Barnwright's value as the default, so the finished building looks exactly like Barnwright's unless a company changes it on purpose.

site._help: What the building sits on. Blocks are laid one per perimeterFtPerBlock feet of outside wall. Anchor counts are an ASSUMPTION (Barnwright never drew anchors): confirm with the shop's master anchor plan.

skids._help: The runners under the floor: treated 4x6 on edge. table gives, per building width in feet, the inches from each side edge to a skid's centre (Alan's build sheet); a width not in the table uses bunk spacing: skids bunkSpacingIn apart, centred, at least 6 in in.

floor._help: Joists run across the width on skids, a rim joist along both long sides, then tongue-and-groove decking. 8 ft wide and smaller use 2x4 joists.

walls._help: Studs on one bottom plate with two top plates; king and jack studs and a header at every opening. Loft (short-wall) studs are 75 in, tall-wall studs 89 in (caption only: the drawn wall height is the style's wallH).

openings._help: Wooden shop-door opening heights by roof shape ('other' for every roof not named): 71 1/2 in on loft (gambrel) builds, 76 1/2 in on tall walls. They are drawn to the nearest ten-thousandth of a foot, as Barnwright does (71.5 in draws as 5.9583 ft). windowTop: on loft builds a window top sits belowWallTopIn under the wall top; on tall walls it is level with the door head, but never closer than minBelowWallTopFt to the wall top.

roof._help: Trusses at spacingIn on centre with plywood gussets. shapes: the roof cross-section numbers by roof shape; {"w": 0.27} means 0.27 times the building width, {"ft": 2.43} a fixed number of feet. rise is the ridge height above the wall top (for the gambrel it is only used to frame the camera and the shadow box -- 0.45W, a kept Barnwright quirk); lowerRise/upperRise/knee are the gambrel's shoulders; ridge is where a saltbox ridge sits across the width; dormerRise is the main roof's rise on a style with a dormer; eaveOverhang is feet along the slope at the -x and +x eaves; cottageEave is the cottage-style eave instead (a level soffit backIn at the back, frontIn at the door side, the roof raised one fascia of fasciaIn); rakeOverhang is the gable-end overhang (a style can override it; a gambrel's is drawn at 0.10 whatever this says, a kept Barnwright quirk).

roofDeck._help: What the roofing is fastened to: purlins (2x4 laid flat) on metal buildings, OSB sheathing otherwise.

loft._help: Loft floor joists on the styles with a loft, at the wall top.

porch._help: Porch posts, deck joists and the rail height.

notes.12: A 12 ft wide building is 11 ft 2 in actual.
notes.14: 14 ft wide needs a permit or pilot car.
